title: Binary Search on a Monotonic Predicate
summary: Search an ordered answer space when a feasibility test changes only once from failing to passing or from passing to failing.
recognition_signals: the answer itself lies in an ordered numeric or discrete range
a candidate can be tested for feasibility
once a candidate passes every larger candidate also passes, or the reverse
core_rules: Establish monotonicity before using binary search.
Search for the exact requested side of the transition, such as the first feasible value.
Keep feasible midpoints when they may still be the minimum feasible answer.
structural_steps: prove or rely on the predicate's monotonic direction
choose lower and upper answer bounds

common_confusions.distinction: Both use boundary-search mechanics. This family is specifically about searching answer values through a monotonic feasibility predicate rather than locating a position in already ordered data.
